Module io.github.brantunger.unruly.core
Package io.github.brantunger.unruly.api

Interface OutputWriter<O>

Type Parameters:
O - The type of the output objects it writes to
Functional Interface:
This is a functional interface and can therefore be used as the assignment target for a lambda expression or method reference.
@FunctionalInterface public interface OutputWriter<O>
Sets a property on the output object. The engine uses it for the properties an action returns with ActionResult.set(java.util.Map), as a language whose expressions have no side effects does. Give an engine one with RulesEngineBuilder.outputWriter(OutputWriter); the default is beansAndMaps().

Implemented by applications, to write to an output object the default writer doesn't suit. A method added to this interface is a default method, so an existing writer keeps compiling and working.

The engine calls it on the thread running the rule, once for each property, in the order the action returned them. What it throws is treated as what an action throws. It fails the rule with a RuleExecutionException naming the rule and the property, which listeners receive in onError; a fatal Error, such as an OutOfMemoryError, is rethrown unchanged once they have. But when the thread was interrupted, or the run passed its deadline, by the time it threw, the run stops, as a cancelled run does, with an exception whose getRuleName() is null, which keeps what it threw as a suppressed exception; unless that is or wraps an Error, which fails the rule all the same. A run that was interrupted, or passed its deadline, while the writer set the properties without throwing stops once every one is set, and they stay set. It must be thread-safe, because runs on many threads share it.

    • beansAndMaps

      static <O> OutputWriter<O> beansAndMaps()
      Returns the default writer. It sets a property with put on a Map output, and otherwise with the output's public setter whose parameter accepts the value, such as setInterestRate for interestRate. A boxed primitive, only when no setter takes it as it is, goes to a setter taking a primitive that Java widens it to, so an Integer reaches a setter taking a long or a double. No value is otherwise converted: never narrowed, so a setter taking an int doesn't accept a Long, and never from one wrapper to another, so a setter taking a Long doesn't accept an Integer. A varargs setter, such as setTags(String...), takes an array: a single value isn't wrapped in one. An output without such a setter fails with IllegalArgumentException, which, for a number, a character or a boolean, names the setters of the property that take a primitive or a wrapper. Of overloaded setters, it calls the most specific one that accepts the value, as Java would; when no single one is the most specific, the choice is fixed for the output class and the same on every run.

      A setter declared with a type variable of a class, such as setContent(T), takes what the output class makes of the variable where the class has another setter of the property with a different parameter: with T a Long, beside setContent(long), a Short goes to setContent(long), as in Java, and text fails.

      Where it differs from Java: a setter declared with a type variable, with no other setter of the property, takes whatever its erased parameter does; a setter whose parameter is a supertype of what the variable is given, such as setContent(CharSequence) beside setContent(T) with T a String, is still tried first, though Java would call setContent(T); an instance of a generic class, such as new Box<Long>(), gives the variable nothing, as its type argument isn't kept at run time, so the setter takes the variable's bound; a type variable an inner class uses from its enclosing class, as in Outer<T>.Inner, isn't resolved, so a setter declared with it, or with a variable it's passed to, takes the variable's bound; and a varargs setter takes only an array.

      The setter is reached the way FactProperties reaches a getter: through a public, exported type that declares it, such as an interface the output class implements, or directly where the class's package is open to io.github.brantunger.unruly.core, which every package on the class path is. A setter it can't reach fails with IllegalStateException, saying what to export or open, rather than a less specific overload being called in its place. One limit: where a class the writer can't reach overrides a generic setter beside another public instance overload of the same name with a narrower parameter, its own or inherited, even from a class that isn't public, a value for that overload reaches the generic setter instead. It fails with an InvocationTargetException caused by a ClassCastException, or, where the overload's parameter is narrower than the generic setter's, the less specific generic setter is called.
